candidateDecisions.label: Predictive business modelling for markets and finance

stoppingDecision.assessment: The first option balances business, mathematics and computing. The second puts more weight on algorithms and mathematical models. The third applies analytics to markets, finance and strategy. The three options differ by at least four courses in each direction. Responsible AI is a further interest and appears within the first and third options through study of AI governance.

analysis: The closest option balances the three defining strands. Mathematical methods, linear algebra and probability underpin statistical and machine-learning work. Python, data science, databases and algorithms give a practical computing sequence. Accounting, econometrics, marketing and empirical customer research provide business applications. UvA runs deterministic and stochastic operations research as two dedicated courses, with further specialist HR, consulting, marketing and analytics project work. The technical option retains substantive business and econometrics and adds C++ and Haskell software development, dynamical systems, multivariable calculus and reinforcement learning. It swaps Deep Learning for the available late optimisation course and studies Advanced Algorithms earlier. It consequently omits the closest option’s text and image modelling specialisation. The markets option instead adds microeconomic decisions, financial assets and banking, international market entry and digital strategy. It studies applied prediction without promising marketing-mix or purchase-propensity model instruction. Across the pairings, social-case analytics, data storytelling, advanced linear algebra, consulting, and stochastic operations research have independent comparator rows. Some content overlaps with UCR methods, including Markov decisions and simulation, but UCR lacks a dedicated operations research sequence. Credit and content boundaries distinguish the two required thesis courses from the optional UCR research element.

alignment.rationale: Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Probability Theory and Statistics 1.

UvA offers a minor, an exchange, electives or an internship combined with electives. The UvA Business Analytics internship carries 12 EC and requires 90 EC already completed.
Both study customer evidence to inform marketing. UvA specifically teaches purchase prediction, choice and marketing-mix models.
UvA requires this 6 EC project alongside the 6 EC Skills course. UCR’s optional research element sits outside the illustrated schedules.
This 6 EC course develops design research and thesis writing alongside the Research Project.

UvA devotes a course to modelling uncertain operations. UCR teaches probabilistic decisions in AI, but has no equivalent operations research sequence in these options.
UvA introduces optimisation and machine learning together through cases about social problems.
